data.name: Chiravansh
data.gender_notes: Chiravansh is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Chiravansh is derived from the Sanskrit words 'chira' meaning eternal and 'vansh' meaning lineage or dynasty. This name is associated with the idea of an eternal and unbroken lineage, often referring to royalty or a noble family heritage. The name Chiravansh carries the meaning “Eternal lineage, dynasty” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Chiravansh usually hope their child will grow to embody eternal lineage, dynasty and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Chiravansh belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Eternal lineage, dynasty.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Chiravansh total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

historical_references.reference: Chiravanshi dynasty was a Rajput dynasty of the Chauhan Rajputs, which ruled over the region of Gujarat, Rajasthan and Malwa during medieval India. The dynasty was founded by Chiravarman, a descendant of the Chauhan chief Bhartrihari.
historical_references.context: The Chiravanshi dynasty ruled over a large territory in western India during the medieval period. The dynasty was founded by Chiravarman, who was a descendant of the Chauhan chief Bhartrihari. The dynasty ruled over the regions of Gujarat, Rajasthan and Malwa.

historical_references.reference: The Chiravanshi Rajputs were a branch of the Chauhan Rajputs who ruled over the area of Jaisalmer in Rajasthan, India. They are believed to have originated from the Chiravarman, who was a descendant of Bhilama Chauhan and a great-grandson of Bhartrihari, the founder of the Chauhan Rajputs.
